grades.quote: LH loads a 16-bit value from memory, then sign-extends to 32-bits before storing in _rd_ . LHU loads a 16-bit value from memory but then zero extends to 32-bits before storing in _rd_ . LB and LBU are defined analogously for 8-bit values.
grades.reason: The RV32I load section says LH sign-extends and LHU zero-extends, and that LB and LBU are defined analogously for 8-bit values. So LB sign-extends the byte and LBU zero-extends it. This directly answers what differs when the top bit is 1.
